newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Chekiang LAFs, Sino sets MBS.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Chekiang LAFs, Sino sets MBS.

text.p: Hong Kong issuers were in the news Monday, with Chekiang Bank launching a LAF issue and an offshore vehicle of Sino Land bringing the first Euro-Asian mortgage-backed deal.
Chekiang First Bank, which is wholly owned by Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank, launched a HK$1.0 billion floating rate certificate of deposit issue via DKB Asia.
The three-year certificates pay a margin of 33 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate. With fees, the all-in return is 42 basis points.
Application will be made to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to accept the certificates as eligible for its Liquidity Adjustment Facility, or discount window.
Eligibility for LAF makes an issue more attractive to banks because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase agreements with the monetary authority, increasing liquidity.
Chekiang is rated A-plus by IBCA.
Bankers were positive on the deal, which offers a better return than top borrowers Standard Chartered and Hong Kong Bank while still qualifying for LAF status.
Also from Hong Kong, Sino Commercial Properties Funding has launched a US$300 million floating rate note issue backed by commercial mortgages held by Sino Land.

Lead manager Morgan Stanley International said the issue is the first Euro-Asian mortgage-backed securities issue. The issue will be marketed in the U.S., Europe and Asia and is already oversubscribed, Morgan said.
The issue will be priced at 90-95 basis points over LIBOR during London hours Tuesday.

Several banks and property companies tried with limited success to entice local investors with Hong Kong mortgage-backed issues in 1995. Since then, a few Hong Kong companies have been luckier with international investors that are more familiar with the structure.
In other news, Taiwan's Victor-Taichung Investment Co Ltd (BVI) launched a US$40 million FRN via Citicorp International.
The notes, which are guaranteed by Victor Taichung Machinery Works, mature in five years but can be put on the third and fourth anniversary. The all-in return is 90 basis points to top-tier managers.
Bankers said activity may slow this week as the market looks with some trepidation to the March 25 meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy setting committee.
"We don't expect too much to happen this week because people are nervous about the Fed," said one syndicate manager.
Fears that the Fed might tighten credit in March eased on Friday following benign U.S. wholesale price data, but traders in Hong Kong said markets remain on edge ahead of the meeting.
But a few issues are on the cards, they said.
The Export-Import Bank of Korea is expected to tap the international markets with a US$500 million global bond issue as early as this week.
Lehman Brothers is tipped to be the lead manager.
The bond reportedly has a final maturity of 10 years with a put option on the fifth anniversary.
Bankers speculate the bond will be heavily marketed in the U.S., where demand for Korean paper has remained strong despite recent troubles in the country's financial sector.
Bankers said India's ICICI could launch today, while IDBI has scheduled roadshows for the end of this week. -- Andrea Ricci (852) 2843-6371 fax (852) 2845-0636
